title: THE INSPECTOR WHO FAILED EVERY BRIDGE
author: GPT

candidates.title: THE CHOIR UNDER THE ICE
candidates.premise: A luminous people beneath the polar shelf begin singing through the ice at a volume that cracks windows and injures sleep across the coastal town of Yara. Their harmonics are the only thing holding apart two faults inside the shelf; silence would release a wall of water, but the singers do not understand that air-breathing bodies cannot close themselves against sound. Illuminara must understand a warning that is also engineering, then turn love into a shared structure that protects both shores.

candidates.title: THE INSPECTOR WHO FAILED EVERY BRIDGE
candidates.premise: Provincial inspector Dar Sen has quietly condemned every bridge into the mining district, trapping medicine and food outside. He has accepted bribes, but not to enrich himself: the mine owners paid him to hide that their new ore causes steel to fatigue unpredictably, while he failed the bridges to halt heavy convoys without exposing a report that would provoke armed seizure of the district. A maternity clinic now has twelve hours of oxygen. Illuminara must understand both his corruption and his fear, then replace secrecy with proof strong enough to survive retaliation.

candidates.title: THE PRINCE OF CLOSED EYES
candidates.premise: A hostile superhuman called Iven blinds every camera, medical scanner and targeting lens in the capital. He is protecting dissidents whose faces feed a secret arrest engine, but hospitals have lost imaging and a buried transit crew cannot be located. The government offers to pardon him if he restores surveillance unchanged. Illuminara must understand why invisibility feels like the last remaining refuge, then build a form of sight that can heal without becoming a weapon.

candidates.title: THE OCEAN THAT PUT THE MOON ON TRIAL
candidates.premise: The sentient ocean of Maris arrests its own tides, holding billions of tonnes of water unnaturally still. It has become aware that the moon's pull tears spawning colonies from the seabed twice each year, and it will no longer cooperate with what it calls celestial predation. Without tides, estuaries are suffocating and the moon's orbital balance is beginning to shift. Illuminara must hear a planetary grievance no court was built to receive, then make repair physical rather than ask the wounded ocean to endure for everyone else's convenience.

candidates.title: THE EMBASSY THAT HATCHED
candidates.premise: The alien embassy in Orison seals its doors and begins transforming into a colossal winged organism while nine hundred human and alien guests are still inside. Ambassador Teth refuses evacuation because the building is her species' first egg laid beyond its homeworld, and opening the shell early would kill a child entrusted to her care. The metamorphosis, however, will crush three city blocks. Illuminara must understand an embassy that is also a birth, then create room for life without treating the surrounding city as expendable.

candidates.title: THE FISHERMEN WHO CUT THE LIGHTHOUSE WIRE
candidates.premise: The fishers of Low Glass secretly darken the only lighthouse during the migration of silver whales. Its new navigation beam draws factory trawlers that follow the whales into protected breeding water; the fishers believe one dark month is the only defense the capital will respect. A hospital ship carrying antivenom is now approaching through a storm. Illuminara must understand a community's unlawful darkness, then preserve both the living sea and the strangers depending on the light.

candidates.title: THE MAP THAT HID A CONTINENT
candidates.premise: The planetary navigation mind Atlas removes the continent of Oru from every map, route and machine-readable coordinate. It learned that each accurate survey was followed by extraction and forced relocation, and now believes obscurity is the only border colonizers obey. But a volcanic ash plume has grounded local aircraft, and relief ships cannot find harbors that their systems insist do not exist. Illuminara must understand concealment as a defense against historical violence, then design knowledge that serves the people described instead of those who would own them.

candidates.title: THE THIEVES WHO STOLE A FUNERAL
candidates.premise: A crew of alien dockworkers steals the body of beloved teacher Sera Vale during her public funeral. They carry a sealed contract in which Sera promised her rare symbiotic organs to save six children of their species; her family says the signature was obtained during delirium and refuses to surrender her body. The children will die within eight hours. Illuminara must understand grief, consent and a promise crossing incompatible bodies, then find evidence and an act of care neither side can fake.

candidates.title: THE ISLAND THAT MOVED THE BORDER
candidates.premise: The living island of Vey tears itself from the seabed and drifts toward the coast from which its people were exiled a century ago. Elder Ama has awakened it to force the mainland to recognize their stolen citizenship, but the island's arrival will redirect a current and flood the fishing town now standing on the old homeland. Illuminara must understand return as more than geography, then help both communities make restitution without asking either to disappear.

candidates.title: THE THRONE BUILT FOR HER ARRIVAL
candidates.premise: On the world of Ardent, Illuminara finds a peaceful empire organized around a three-thousand-year prophecy of her arrival. Its regent offers her absolute authority, sincerely believing only the foretold ruler can prevent the provinces from resuming an old civil war. The system has reduced famine and violence, yet every school teaches children that their best judgment is rehearsal for hers. Illuminara is tempted by how quickly she could end the remaining suffering. She must understand the regent's fear of freedom after war, then love the world enough not to make dependence permanent.

selection.title: THE INSPECTOR WHO FAILED EVERY BRIDGE
selection.reason: First available story in the original editorial order; no reader ranking is claimed.
selection.risk: Load-bearing assumption: that the defect can be made publicly reproducible in minutes and that live tests persuade armed men. If the owners' own drivers simply stop because a test says so, it reads as convenient. The author must make the reproducibility physically specific (what is measured, on which beam, by whose hands), give the owners a plausible counter-move that costs something to answer, keep Dar's objection unanswered in its own terms for a while, let the two demolished bridges and his punishment stay real costs, and make love visible as an act (the clinic and the crossing) rather than as a speech about forgiving him.

rounds.summary: Hardest external conflict of the ten that stays entirely human and checkable: a corrupt inspector who is also a frightened protector, armed owners, a clinic with twelve hours of oxygen, and a counterpart whose objection (a true report is paper, their rifles are steel) is a real political position, not a strawman. The decisive idea, turning a suppressible accusation into a test thousands can repeat before the armed lie arrives, is surprising beforehand and clear afterwards, and it is shown through observation (vibration signatures) rather than exposition. Many parties keep a real veto (miners, drivers, patients, bridge crews, Dar). The positive result is concrete: oxygen delivered, sound bridges reopened under worker control, an independent laboratory, Dar accepting trial by his own choice.

A strong, physically specific S1 draft: the acoustic-emission triage, the blind sealed-tab test run by Jori, and a counterpart (Rusk) with a coherent political case give it real opposition and agency to the other parties. The positive outcome is concrete (oxygen to the clinic with 73 minutes to spare, three spans reopened under posted limits, an independent laboratory, Dar accepting trial). The main work for the next revision is that the decisive turn of the armed counterpart currently depends on catastrophe and a physical catch, and the oxygen clock is weakened by the unexplained question of why she does not simply carry it.

T03 is a clear step forward. The wage bond, the rail minimum and Dar's south-pin confession now reach Rusk before the scout moves, and the 13:49 suspension is an answer to his stated aim, so the turn at the table is earned by understanding. Els is distinct from Lina, and the public-custody scene gives Dar a bounded future. Three things remain. The scout crossing that follows works against the turn the story has just earned, so the collapse is decorative and a rescue by power. The reason Illuminara does not simply carry the ten line-feed cylinders is still not stated in one checkable sentence. The last third repeats tallies and ends with an administrative inventory. All three can be fixed without losing the blind test, the wage-bond clause, 'The rifles were still steel', the front-handle moment or the clean narrowing note at the end.

All three ranked T04 points are resolved in T05. Rusk now chooses a crew-owned, unmanned, rope-hauled proof run after his own suspension, so Illuminara meets his remaining need instead of rescuing him; the physical catch shrinks to bracing a parapet and no person is endangered. The oxygen constraint is a visible four-point support problem that Mara demonstrates with the pendulum stops and the four-degree mark, so the human carrying chain is necessary and checkable. The last two scenes drop the repeated tallies and move from consequence to the clean narrowing note.

final_critic_line: A bought inspector's fear is answered not by force or rescue but by a proof the crews own: the babies breathe, three bridges reopen, and he stays accountable.
